description: #5057 — the WRITER the `query_page_aliases` fixture left waived: `set_page_aliases`, the only thing that puts rows in `page_aliases`. That table is outside the snapshot's five arrays, so what each op wrote is observed by the `get_page_aliases` steps rather than by the settled state — and the RETURN carries evidence of its own, because the command answers with the rows it actually INSERTED, which is narrower than what the caller passed. Four behaviours the mock got wrong, all found here: it stored the caller's array verbatim, so `  spaced  ` kept its padding, the two empty entries became alias rows, an alias another page already held was stolen from it, and a page id naming no live page was accepted instead of refused. The backend trims, skips what trims to nothing, and writes `INSERT OR IGNORE` against a `UNIQUE ... COLLATE NOCASE` index, so a taken alias is silently dropped from both the table and the answer; the page probe runs inside the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and raises `NotFound` (#661). The replacement is TOTAL — a DELETE precedes the inserts — which is why S1's seeded `keep-me` is gone after the first op and why re-listing an alias the page already held is not a self-conflict with itself. `S2` is the conflict owner and never writes, so the `aliases_of_conflict_owner_unchanged` step is what separates 'skipped' from 'stolen': a mock that let the claim through leaves S2 empty. The `replacement_reclaims_its_own_alias` op is where the DELETE-before-INSERT ordering is pinned rather than merely implied: S3 re-lists the alias it already holds, which only survives because its old row is gone by then. NOT pinned: an EMPTY alias list, whose whole correct answer is `[]` — the #4670 guard refuses a command-leg record carrying neither a return nor a refusal, because such a record compares nothing, and no input makes this command answer non-empty while clearing. The DELETE it would pin is covered twice over by `keep-me` vanishing and by the self-reclaim above. Also not pinned: alias propagation between devices — `page_aliases` is deliberately outside the op log (there is no `SetPageAliases` `OpPayload`), so the digest below stays empty and a sync test is the wrong shape for it.
name: page_alias_writes

ops.comment: Six entries, two rows. `  spaced  ` is trimmed to `spaced`; `` and `   ` trim to nothing and are skipped; `taken` belongs to S2 and the `INSERT OR IGNORE` drops it; `fresh` lands and `FRESH` then collides with it under the NOCASE index, so only the first spelling survives. The answer is `spaced`, `fresh` — in the order given, not sorted. A mock echoing its argument answers all six and reddens on the first token.
ops.name: trims_skips_empties_and_drops_taken

ops.comment: S3 already holds `stale`, and re-listing it is NOT a self-conflict: the DELETE runs before the inserts, so the row is gone by the time it is re-claimed. A backend that inserted without deleting first answers `extra` alone. `STALE` then collides with the `stale` this very call just took, so the in-call dedup is the same NOCASE index, not a separate rule. The answer is `stale`, `extra`.
ops.name: replacement_reclaims_its_own_alias

ops.comment: S4 is a `content` block, not a `page`. The probe is `block_type = 'page' AND deleted_at IS NULL`, so this is `NotFound` and nothing is written — the step below shows `orphan` reached no page. The mock accepted it and filed the aliases under a non-page id.
ops.name: refuses_a_non_page_id

queries.comment: `fresh`, `spaced` — sorted, so this is not the return order re-read. The seeded `keep-me` is GONE: the write replaces the whole set. `  spaced  ` is here trimmed; `taken`, `FRESH` and the two empties never landed.
queries.name: aliases_after_replacement

queries.comment: S2 never wrote, and still holds `taken`: S1's claim was SKIPPED, not honoured. A mock that let the claim through moves the row and answers empty here.
queries.name: aliases_of_conflict_owner_unchanged

queries.comment: `extra`, `stale` — sorted. The seed gave S3 `stale` alone, so `extra` is new and `stale` survived being re-listed exactly once: no duplicate row, and none lost to a self-conflict.
queries.name: aliases_after_self_reclaim

queries.comment: `orphan` resolves to nothing: the refused op wrote no row anywhere, not merely none S4 can be read back through. `Global` applies no space filter, so a miss here is a miss everywhere.
queries.name: refused_alias_reached_no_page

queries.comment: The trimmed form is the row: `SPACED` matches it under the NOCASE index and answers S1. A mock that stored `  spaced  ` verbatim misses, because the padding is part of the stored text and no collation folds it away.
queries.name: trimmed_alias_is_what_resolves
